[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Linear Algebra with numpy.linalg in NumPy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Linear algebra is the foundation of many data science and machine learning algorithms. NumPy provides a dedicated submodule called numpy.linalg to perform standard matrix and vector operations efficiently."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Matrix Multiplication and Dot Products"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into linalg specific functions, it is important to remember how to multiply matrices. While the asterisk operator performs element-wise multiplication, the np.dot() function or the @ operator performs true matrix multiplication."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np

A = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
B = np.array([[5, 6], [7, 8]])

# Matrix multiplication
C = np.dot(A, B)
# Alternatively using the @ operator
C_alt = A @ B
print(C)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Finding the Inverse of a Matrix"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The inverse of a square matrix A is denoted as A^(-1) such that multiplying A by its inverse yields the identity matrix. You can use np.linalg.inv() to compute this."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"A_inv = np.linalg.inv(A)
print(A_inv)

# Verifying the inverse (A @ A_inv should be close to identity)
identity_check = np.dot(A, A_inv)
print(np.round(identity_check))"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Solving Linear Equation Systems"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can solve systems of linear equations of the form Ax = b using the np.linalg.solve() function. This is numerically more stable than explicitly computing the inverse of A."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Coefficients matrix A and dependent variable vector b
A = np.array([[3, 1], [1, 2]])
b = np.array([9, 8])

# Solve for x
x = np.linalg.solve(A, b)
print('Solution x:', x)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Eigenvalues and eigenvectors are crucial in dimensionality reduction techniques like Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The function np.linalg.eig() returns a tuple containing the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eig(A)
print('Eigenvalues:', eigenvalues)
print('Eigenvectors:\n', eigenvectors)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Matrix Norms and Determinants"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"np.linalg.det(A): Computes the determinant of a square matrix."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"np.linalg.norm(A): Calculates the matrix or vector norm."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"det_A = np.linalg.det(A)
norm_A = np.linalg.norm(A)
print('Determinant:', det_A)
print('Norm:', norm_A)"}]
